# BTicino C300X Integration v2.2.0

## 2026-11-14

More useful native display controls, clearer configuration and improved
recovery when connections, recordings or agent updates are interrupted.

## Native Display

- Configure connection, media, activations, Alarmo, display, pages and tiles
  in separate settings areas. Each tile has its own size, name and secondary
  line, with translated field labels and help.
- Arrange up to eight pages. Page names and connection status move into the
  header, leaving more space for tiles. Weather heads the status page; Alarmo
  and its optional quick action have their own setup step.
- Control locks, vacuums, valves, humidifiers and water heaters where the
  entity supports it. Unlocking or opening a lock requires a second tap;
  leaving the page, sleeping or losing the action clears the confirmation.
- Show automations and sirens as switch tiles, and people and device trackers
  as read-only tiles. Type symbols and local timestamps improve readability.
- Media players have a compact transport row, artist information and supported
  shuffle/repeat controls. Lights offer effects and fans follow their speed grid.
- Keep cleared fields empty after validation errors, preserve existing untitled
  pages and Alarmo settings when Display patch is disabled, and refresh display
  events immediately after an agent restart.

## Calls, Recordings and Recovery

- Improve WebRTC startup and teardown, preserve early ICE candidates, restore
  ring previews after returning to the card, and handle interrupted audio setup.
- Coordinate talkback startup with media shutdown, reclaim completed workers
  and honor the advertised RTSP timeout for Ring and Home Call playback.
- Preserve finished recordings and earlier clips on failed attempts. Clean up
  cancelled workspaces and reject busy audio captures before answering a call.
- Bound speech-analysis transmission, response and cleanup times. Completed
  captures remain successful when late call events or keepalive failures arrive.
- Recover unavailable entities and memo/message lists after reconnects without
  idle polling. Large memo lists transfer within a fixed shared output budget.
- Retry unfinished update steps and verify repair outcomes against device
  status. SSH reinstalls preserve device-owned settings. Staged update chunks
  no longer trigger a flash sync each time; installed files still sync safely.
- Preserve customized blueprints, queued commands and pending configuration.

## Security and Compatibility

- Keep saved keys out of configuration forms, redact diagnostic addresses and
  bound debug output. Empty key fields retain existing credentials.
- Validate addresses, ports, numeric values and message IDs. Reject malformed
  webhook credentials and clean up registrations after interrupted setup.
- Limit HTTP/RTSP resource usage, reserve incoming connections for the local
  display, validate configured RTSP credentials and clear session keys on stop.
- Verify routing backups and release archive contents before using them.
- RTSP uses TCP interleaving; unsupported UDP requests receive an explicit
  rejection. Home Assistant already uses TCP. See the [security policy](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
  for local-network requirements and separate RTSP credential limitations.

## Upgrade

- **Update the native agent to 2.2.0** through the offered Repair after updating
  the integration. The release includes a rebuilt agent and new display files;
  updating Home Assistant alone does not apply device-side fixes.
- Reapplying an active Display patch restarts the device GUI once.
- Home Assistant **2026.7.0** remains the minimum. Keep existing entries and cards.
- Validation uses local automated tests and ARMHF builds. No new physical-device
  installation or hardware interoperability test is claimed for this candidate.
